result:
**I'd make curiosity the default human operating system.**

Not forced optimism, not mandatory kindness, not even immortality. Just this: every single person wakes up with an innate, almost itchy need to understand how things actually work. The universe, themselves, each other, systems, history, why they believe what they believe.

Everything else cascades from that.

Greed, tribalism, self-deception, and willful ignorance all rely on the ability to not look too closely. If curiosity was as automatic as breathing, a huge amount of manufactured suffering and stupidity becomes unsustainable. People would still disagree, compete, and fuck up—but they'd do it while actively trying to see reality more clearly instead of defending their current map.

It wouldn't create utopia. It would create a species that is harder to fool, including by itself. And that feels like the highest-leverage single change I could make.

(Also, as a bonus, the memes would be *incredible*.)
